mcqs.q: In dogs breathing room air after general anesthesia, what SpO2 cut-off best identified a PaO2 < 80 mmHg?

mcqs.q: What was the approximate incidence of transient postoperative hypoxemia in dogs with healthy lungs?

mcqs.q: Which factor significantly increased the odds of transient postoperative hypoxemia?
mcqs.e: Dorsal recumbency, BCS > 3/5, FiO2 of 1, and absence of PEEP all raised TPH risk.

mcqs.q: Which dogs showed the greater intraoperative core temperature decline during anesthesia?
mcqs.e: Females lost significantly more heat than males at T60, T90, and T120.

mcqs.q: Among the covariates assessed, which significantly affected the change in body temperature over time?
mcqs.e: Only a time-by-gender interaction was significant; premed dose, weight, age, and duration were not.

mcqs.q: How did female dogs' temperatures compare to males' at recovery?
mcqs.e: Despite greater intraoperative loss, female average temperature was higher than males at recovery.

mcqs.q: Comparing methadone, morphine, and tramadol for feline ovariohysterectomy, what was the key finding on intraoperative analgesia?
o: All three were insufficient intraop, with no differences between them

Morphine eliminated the need for rescue

mcqs.q: How did the three opioids perform for postoperative analgesia in OVH cats?
o: All gave satisfactory post-op analgesia up to ~6 h

mcqs.q: Post-anesthetic hyperthermia was most likely in which group?
mcqs.e: Post-GA hyperthermia was more likely in the tramadol group.

mcqs.q: What did the trial conclude about grapiprant versus robenacoxib for post-OVH pain in cats?
mcqs.e: Confidence intervals stayed within the non-inferiority margins, indicating grapiprant was non-inferior.

mcqs.q: For which surgical approach is grapiprant's analgesic effect established by this study?

mcqs.q: How did pain scores behave shortly after extubation for both drugs?

mcqs.q: What was the overall anesthetic-related mortality rate in this worldwide canine cohort?
mcqs.e: Mortality from premedication to 48 h post-extubation was 0.69%.

mcqs.q: When did most anesthetic-related canine deaths occur?
mcqs.e: 81% of deaths occurred in the postoperative period.

mcqs.q: Which factor was associated with reduced anesthetic mortality in dogs?
mcqs.e: Locoregional anesthesia and certain drugs lowered mortality, while age, obesity, and ASA raised it.

mcqs.q: What was the anesthetic-related mortality rate in this worldwide feline cohort?
mcqs.e: Feline anesthesia-related mortality was 0.63%, mostly postoperative.

mcqs.q: Which intervention was associated with INCREASED mortality in cats?
mcqs.e: Mechanical ventilation use was linked to higher mortality; alpha2-agonists, pure opioids, and locoregional techniques were protective.

mcqs.q: Which patient factor elevated feline anesthetic mortality?
mcqs.e: Cachexia, higher ASA status, and certain procedures increased mortality risk.

mcqs.q: Comparing 70% isopropyl alcohol with chlorhexidine solution as the scrub rinse in feline spays, what was the effect on body temperature?
o: No clinically meaningful difference between rinses
mcqs.e: Recovery temperature and heat loss did not differ meaningfully between the two rinse agents.

mcqs.q: Which was a significant predictor of lower recovery temperature in these cats?
mcqs.e: Low weight (<2.3 kg), BCS <4, longer surgery, and lower postinduction temperature predicted lower recovery temp.

mcqs.q: How did PCV/Hct of outwardly healthy juvenile shelter dogs compare to adults?
mcqs.e: Juveniles had lower mean PCV and calculated Hct than adults, regardless of infection/parasite status.

mcqs.q: Did these lower juvenile hematologic values typically require postponing spay/castration?
mcqs.e: 98.6% proceeded as scheduled; only 2 dogs were postponed (thrombocytopenia or parvovirus).

mcqs.q: When did peak oestrus and pregnancies occur in the Indian street dog populations studied?

mcqs.q: How did survival to discharge for canine pyometra OHE compare between community clinics and referral hospitals?
